entries.title: Finite-domain Kalikow directional drift
entries.statement: For an iid uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbour RWRE, let U be a finite connected domain containing 0 and x, T_U its first exit, G_U^omega(0,x)=E_omega^0[sum_(n<T_U) 1_(X_n=x)], and d_ell(omega(x))=sum_e omega(x,e)(e dot ell). The finite-domain Kalikow directional drift at x is E[G_U^omega(0,x)d_ell(omega(x))]/E[G_U^omega(0,x)]. The weighting by the Green function depends on the site's kernel.
assumptions: finite connected U contains 0 and x
iid site law for the conditional expectation statement

entries.title: DRAFT: Nonnegative local drift gives a uniform occupation bound
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent review pending. For every iid nearest-neighbour environment on Z^d, d>=2, with all transitions >=kappa>0, and a unit ell such that d_ell(p)>=0 almost surely and m=E[d_ell(p)]>0, every finite connected U containing 0 and x has E[G_U(0,x)d_ell(omega(x))]/E[G_U(0,x)] >= kappa*m/[1-(2d-1)kappa]. In particular E_0[(X_(T_U)-X_0) dot ell] >= this constant times E_0[T_U].
assumptions: nonnegative local directional drift almost surely

entries.title: DRAFT: Quantitative rare-positive-bias special case
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent review pending. Let d>=2, a=1/(2d), 0<b<a and theta in (0,1]. At iid sites choose the balanced row p0(e)=a with probability 1-theta and row p+(+e1)=a+b, p+(-e1)=a-b, p+(e)=a transversely with probability theta. Every finite-domain Kalikow drift in e1 is at least 2*b*theta/[1+(1-theta)*b/a]. The bound is sharp over arbitrary nonnegative exit vectors q, with no assertion of geometric or speed sharpness. The standard Kalikow criterion and L5 give a deterministic velocity with v dot e1 at least that bound. At theta=0 or b=0 the e1 speed is zero.
assumptions: iid binary site kernels as explicitly stated
standard Kalikow implication used only for velocity existence

entries.title: DRAFT: Discounted occupation bound transfers to velocity
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent review pending. For a law satisfying L2 or L3 and admitting an almost-sure deterministic velocity v, the corresponding uniform occupation-drift lower bound c also satisfies v dot ell>=c. Proof uses discounted single-site Green functions and an Abelian limit; it needs no separate regeneration moment assumption. Velocity existence for these restricted laws follows from the standard Kalikow-to-ballisticity theorem, treated as an external dependency.

entries.title: Refuted auxiliary bridge: positive mean implies positive Kalikow drift
entries.statement: REFUTED PROPOSED BRIDGE, not a theorem: the proposed universal implication is that in an iid uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbour environment on Z^2, E[d_e1(omega(0))]>0 forces positive finite-domain Kalikow e1 drift at every x in every finite connected U containing 0. The explicit two-site example in this bundle contradicts that implication. This refuted bridge has no directional transience hypothesis and is distinct from C0041.
assumptions: hypothetical iid UE law on Z^2

entries.title: DRAFT: Exact iid two-site obstruction to a mean-drift bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT; author counterexample, independent review pending. In an iid UE environment on Z^2 with rows p+=(9/20,1/20,1/4,1/4) and p-=(1/20,9/20,1/4,1/4), P(p+)=51/100, the mean e1 local drift is 1/125>0, but the annealed Kalikow drift at x=0 in U={0,-e1}, starting at 0, is -62753/3982809<0. For general type probability theta the signed numerator has sign 31280*theta^2+223282*theta-127281, giving exactly the negative-drift interval 1/2<theta<theta_star, with theta_star in (53/100,531/1000). This is a counterexample to a mean-drift-to-Kalikow bridge; no directional transience claim is made for this law.
assumptions: no premise or conclusion about full-walk directional transience

entries.title: C0041: Historical question and unverified recent resolution claim
entries.statement: STATUS NOTE 2026-10-10: C0041 asks whether iid uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbour RWRE on Z^d, d>=2, that is annealed almost surely transient in a fixed direction must be ballistic in that direction. The 2013 source is Open question 2.20 (PDF p.24, printed p.22). The stored September-7 search is dated. A September-23-2026 public manuscript and separate Lean proof entrypoint claim the full conclusion; no independent rebuild or transitive trusted-axiom receipt was obtained here. Current openness UNKNOWN. Do not confuse the admitted comparator statement with the separate proof or mark C0041 solved from a source/hash check.
assumptions: no parent-target proof certified by w450

relations.rationale: The conclusion bounds exactly the occupation-weighted ratio in the definition.
The binary balanced/positive-drift law has nonnegative local drift and permits a stronger exact ratio bound.
The velocity lower bound uses the discounted transfer after the standard criterion gives a velocity.
The finite-domain ratio proof extends to discounted Green functions and an Abelian velocity limit.
Both ends refer to iid UE Z^2; mean drift 1/125 is positive, but the specific finite-domain Kalikow drift is -62753/3982809.
The computed negative quantity is exactly the defined finite-domain occupation ratio.
Adds a dated source-status caution to the exact existing target without asserting a proof or refutation.
